evidence_note: Local sources inspected; recorded proof claims are not freshly replayed in this inventory. Latest builder reports are explicitly distinguished from independent acceptance.

candidates.title: Slow command filters with useful forced tracking
candidates.question: Can a causal slow command filter meet the fixed 0.2 mm tracking task while reducing actual jerk or command variation relative to direct control?
candidates.prior_work: A common quadratic certificate supports unforced slow-filter stability; later exact-integer Taylor enclosures report violations for both fixed forced filters. Those enclosures are not Lean checked.
candidates.obstacle: Unforced stability does not imply useful forced tracking; moving endpoints or granting preview changes the task.
candidates.crossover_seed: Borrow frequency-weighted model reduction and disturbance-observer residual cancellation, treating filter memory as a state.
candidates.cheap_test: Derive the augmented transfer function and compare its low-frequency moments against direct feedback before any gain search.

candidates.title: Choose feedforward for the actual performance objective
candidates.question: Which jerk-feedforward coefficient minimizes finite-horizon position error rather than the invariant-cube residual or initial jerk error?
candidates.prior_work: Two different minimax objectives yield 5/(48 sigma) and 1/(10 sigma); numerical short-move cases can favor no jerk feedforward.
candidates.obstacle: A certificate-optimal coefficient can be poor on the real task; varying-rate worst cases are not established.
candidates.crossover_seed: Import robust approximation equioscillation and horizon-weighted optimal transport of impulse-response mass.
candidates.cheap_test: For a fixed polynomial reference compute exact low-order error series for the three coefficients and locate the horizon where their ranking reverses.

candidates.title: Causal high-order reference feasibility
candidates.question: Can a compact admission rule reject impossible endpoint/deadline requests with bounded jerk, snap and latency before controller synthesis?
candidates.prior_work: An exact lower bound T >= a0/J + 2J/S rejects a prior endpoint; a different causal 0.6 m task has an explicit feasible polynomial reference.
candidates.obstacle: Zero acceleration is not zero velocity; preserving a full endpoint is stricter than delaying one event.
candidates.crossover_seed: Treat derivative-constrained reachability as a moment problem with positive integration kernels and dual certificates.
candidates.cheap_test: Derive simultaneous lower bounds on position and velocity from the extremal jerk profile and compare to the saved rejected endpoint.

candidates.title: Co-design digital hold gains and information age
candidates.question: Can the fixed digital-hold controller admit a materially larger total information age without widening the declared clearance tube?
candidates.prior_work: The later C3/C7 packets report derived mixed-history budgets and finite constructed holding at 1 ms total age; older planning notes are superseded for that milestone.
candidates.obstacle: The sufficient budget has little slack and gain changes alter both sensor amplification and contraction.
candidates.crossover_seed: Use robust co-design as a small-gain loop between age-induced state error and feedback slope.
candidates.cheap_test: Express the two-pass age inequality symbolically in gains and identify whether reducing slope increases admitted age after retaining the same cube.

candidates.title: Sharp stopping clearance from transient structure
candidates.question: Can the derived-loss rate-floor model obtain a reusable tight clearance formula rather than a loose polynomial relaxation or one numerical instance?
candidates.prior_work: Builder packet reports an exact 0.142 m peak certificate through first zero versus a 0.1605859375 m relaxed formula; binary64 peak is about 0.1407108 m. Independent acceptance is not inferred here.
candidates.obstacle: General parameter dependence and certified near-tightness remain separate from one fixed certificate.
candidates.crossover_seed: Use convex dual envelopes and optimal stopping: certify the velocity-root bracket and optimize only the corresponding position interval.
candidates.cheap_test: On the saved instance derive a rational root bracket from monotone velocity and bound the position slack inside it.

candidates.title: Whole-region recovery controller comparison
candidates.question: When braking and direct feedback share the same initial box and plant assumptions, which has the larger certified recovery region per checking cost?
candidates.prior_work: A 25-step direct-feedback pilot is checked for one rate/state cell with a robust tail; the full initial-box/rate covering is not checked.
candidates.obstacle: Single-cell wins and endpoint-only comparisons cannot establish whole-region superiority.
candidates.crossover_seed: Borrow branch-and-bound proof reuse and abstraction refinement: refine only cells whose certificates fail.
candidates.cheap_test: Identify a pair of neighboring cells sharing valid coefficient bounds and test whether one terminal certificate can cover their union.

candidates.title: Sample-interval certificate conservatism
candidates.question: How much allowable sampling range is lost to Bernstein/LDL certificates compared with true held-map stability on the same normalized plant?
candidates.prior_work: Exact rational producer and Lean checker support interval energy decrease; a wider double-integrator variant reaches h=33/50 with smaller margin.
candidates.obstacle: Failure of the chosen common quadratic or Bernstein coefficient test is not instability.
candidates.crossover_seed: Use polynomial approximation subdivision and common-metric geometry to separate representation conservatism from metric conservatism.
candidates.cheap_test: For the 2-state benchmark compute the exact Schur stability polynomial and compare its boundary to the stored certificate interval.

candidates.title: Reusable certificates on a genuinely different plant
candidates.question: Can an independent second plant use the unchanged interval-certificate interface with less manual proof work than a fresh bespoke derivation?
candidates.prior_work: Jerk, planar and actuator-lag benchmarks exist, but independent downstream reuse and quantitative engineering advantage are unestablished.
candidates.obstacle: Another rescaling of the same model is not evidence of reusable abstraction.
candidates.crossover_seed: Transfer proof-carrying compilation: separate a small semantic model adapter from a generic untrusted producer and checker.
candidates.cheap_test: Take the existing coupled-planar benchmark, list its model-specific proof obligations, and test whether its generated certificate can be consumed unchanged by the common interface.

candidates.title: Safe excitation for coupled-source identifiability
candidates.question: Can a bounded intervention distinguish wheel imbalance from synchronous drivetrain forcing enough to change a safe control decision?
candidates.prior_work: A source survey and a fixed synthetic exact-rational example show duplicate/trial readings need not identify baseline contribution; a separating reading can shrink the retained set.
candidates.obstacle: Known trial sensitivity alone does not identify baseline imbalance; dynamic plant/interface and phase errors are absent.
candidates.crossover_seed: Use dual control and causal experimental design: optimize information gain subject to robust action envelopes.
candidates.cheap_test: Construct the rank-deficient two-source observation map, then add one phase/order-separating row and quantify feasible-set width under bounded error.

candidates.title: Finite-horizon tracking bounds beyond invariant cubes
candidates.question: Can a finite-horizon tube certify the short-move task that a global invariant cube makes excessively conservative?
candidates.prior_work: Invariant-cube tracking and finite polynomial-reference comparisons exist; exact Taylor enclosures demonstrate a practical path to finite-time bounds.
candidates.obstacle: An all-time cube discards transient cancellations; sampled numerical passes are not continuous enclosures.
candidates.crossover_seed: Import finite-time reachability and energy localization with a time-varying storage function.
candidates.cheap_test: Propagate a small interval state through one saved polynomial phase and compare its position envelope to the fixed R tube without changing the task.

candidates.title: Active-facet geometry for invariant entry
candidates.question: Can active-facet geometry yield a less conservative full-state entry test than independent box bounds for the tilted hold cube?
candidates.prior_work: The milestone packet explicitly defers family 149 active-facet entry; C3 derives a tilted-coordinate guard and exposes exact widening failures.
candidates.obstacle: Shared physical coordinates couple the facets; independent coordinate extrema may be unattainable together.
candidates.crossover_seed: Borrow polyhedral contact geometry and complementary slackness to characterize only reachable active-face combinations.
candidates.cheap_test: Enumerate signed active facets of the 3D tilted cube and find which combinations are feasible under the saved sensor and pending-command bounds.

candidates.title: Separate actuator response rate from authority loss
candidates.question: What minimal varying-rate and effective-target model captures meaningful stopping variability without disguising reduced braking strength as slower response?
candidates.prior_work: Comparison envelopes support varying rate and target; earlier fixed-rate results cannot model changed steady acceleration or friction-brake modes merely by widening lag.
candidates.obstacle: No calibrated mechanism or data validates a particular rate/target uncertainty set.
candidates.crossover_seed: Use dimensional analysis and set-membership identification to expose independently observable rate and authority directions.
candidates.cheap_test: Construct equal-time-constant models with different steady acceleration and test the saved clearance contract on both; then identify the missing authority premise.

candidates.title: From finite constructed handoff to ongoing execution
candidates.question: Can the finite recovery/detector/pending/hold construction be extended consistently to one infinite non-Zeno execution with the same safety ceiling?
candidates.prior_work: C7/C8 builder packets construct arbitrary finite horizons and preserve the actual prefix, readings and clock; infinite execution remains explicitly open.
candidates.obstacle: Compatible finite horizons and prefix agreement must be proved, rather than extending a finite formula outside its theorem domain.
candidates.crossover_seed: Use projective-limit style prefix consistency or stream coinduction with a positive clock step.
candidates.cheap_test: Compare the N and N+1 recurrences symbolically on their common horizon and identify the exact index-stability lemma needed.

candidates.title: Detector correctness under variable dispatch latency
candidates.question: Can first qualifying sampled readings remain causally linked to the switched plant when dispatch latency varies and messages can tie or reorder?
candidates.prior_work: C6 proves finite guard detection on a 0.5 ms grid with common latency; it retains explicit counterexamples for tied dispatches and excessive age.
candidates.obstacle: Common latency gives strict arrival order; arbitrary variable delays do not.
candidates.crossover_seed: Transfer distributed-systems causal clocks and sequence-number monotonicity into the hybrid controller contract.
candidates.cheap_test: Construct two bounded-latency readings that arrive out of order and test a latest-timestamp-only acceptance rule against the age bound.

candidates.title: Machine arithmetic to real-valued control theorem
candidates.question: What error contract lets a finite-word implementation inherit the real-valued clipped controller guarantee, including overflow and rounding?
candidates.prior_work: Ideal nearest-grid rounding is proved over mathematical reals; machine arithmetic and deployed executable correspondence are explicitly excluded.
candidates.obstacle: Rounding, clamp order and overflow can violate the assumed error channel.
candidates.crossover_seed: Borrow sound abstract interpretation and proof-carrying compilation with outward interval arithmetic.
candidates.cheap_test: Evaluate one control expression over boundary-state intervals using a declared fixed-point format and derive an exact worst rounding/overflow bound.

candidates.title: Complete model-bound certificate acceptance
candidates.question: Can a certificate checker reject incomplete coverage, changed model semantics and stale artifacts without trusting the producer?
candidates.prior_work: Producer/model negative controls exist; a prior source-attribution checker was repaired after omitted stage/branch/action cases could narrow its domain.
candidates.obstacle: Mathematical validity of supplied branches does not prove all required branches were supplied.
candidates.crossover_seed: Use typed manifests as proof obligations and finite-cover certificates borrowed from exhaustive model checking.
candidates.cheap_test: Delete one required branch from a copied in-memory certificate and verify that coverage fails before any accepted summary can be emitted.

candidates.title: Within-hold disturbance semantics
candidates.question: Can the fixed held-error safety theorem tolerate bounded within-hold forcing without silently reusing constant-input formulas?
candidates.prior_work: Fixed-lag execution uses held command-equivalent errors; a separate varying-response comparison handles continuous effective targets for finite envelopes.
candidates.obstacle: Constant-flow equalities and all-time energy certificates do not automatically transfer to arbitrary forcing.
candidates.crossover_seed: Use integral quadratic constraints or convolution-kernel L1 bounds to translate the disturbance history into a checked step residual.
candidates.cheap_test: Compute the exact impulse-response sign pattern on one hold and compare constant worst-case forcing with a sign-aligned bounded forcing.

candidates.title: Own-state quantization and execution uniqueness
candidates.question: Can existence and uniqueness be established for the sampled controller with deterministic state-dependent quantization rather than prescribed error sequences?
candidates.prior_work: Uniqueness is proved for prescribed h,e,d; a nominal ideal-rounding theorem is separate and does not supply the requested uncertain execution claim.
candidates.obstacle: An arbitrary bounded error sequence and a deterministic quantizer are different closed-loop interfaces.
candidates.crossover_seed: Use hybrid transition systems: evaluate quantization at sample boundaries, then solve a unique smooth held flow.
candidates.cheap_test: Write the deterministic sample recurrence and check that a tie-breaking convention yields a unique next state even at quantizer boundaries.

candidates.title: Saturation certificate scope and hidden inactive regimes
candidates.question: Can a robust invariant include genuinely active clipping throughout a region without relying on a budget that secretly forces clipping inactive?
candidates.prior_work: The local rounded-controller budget is proved to exclude clipping; a different actuator-lag travel ellipsoid includes active clipping and a separate finite recovery trace exists.
candidates.obstacle: Reusing the local budget as evidence for a broad saturated basin changes the proved statement.
candidates.crossover_seed: Use complementarity/sector partitions and piecewise storage functions tied to actual clamp modes.
candidates.cheap_test: Find the exact intersection of each candidate invariant with the active-clamp halfspaces and reject any advertised clipping result with empty intersection.

candidates.title: Diagnose mismatch while a safe fallback remains reachable
candidates.question: Can a runtime model monitor detect a specific actuator fault early enough that a certified fallback is still available?
candidates.prior_work: The reviews distinguish logical fault detection, diagnostic coverage and complete stopping assurance; no local fault-to-fallback timing guarantee is supplied.
candidates.obstacle: Detecting a model violation after the recoverable set has been left offers no safety guarantee.
candidates.crossover_seed: Combine change detection with backward reachability: monitor threshold is constrained by the remaining backup reserve.
candidates.cheap_test: For a declared bounded authority-loss fault, compare earliest distinguishable residual time with the latest safe brake-switch time.

candidates.title: Common-cause failures at the proof/reliability interface
candidates.question: How can deterministic execution guarantees be composed with an explicit fault process without pretending proof success establishes a safety performance level?
candidates.prior_work: Prior review separates functional behavior, dangerous failure frequency and architecture/validation obligations; no component reliability data or PL claim exists.
candidates.obstacle: A per-stop exceedance probability cannot be converted to an hourly failure rate without an operational model; shared causes defeat independent multiplication.
candidates.crossover_seed: Borrow fault-tree cut sets and adversarial causal graphs to make shared sensor/clock/power assumptions visible.
candidates.cheap_test: Build a minimal symbolic two-channel fault model with one shared cause and show the gap between independent and common-cause failure calculations.

candidates.title: Population uncertainty to a conditional envelope
candidates.question: What evidence contract converts multi-unit, repeated-condition stopping data into a calibrated uncertainty set while retaining separate statistical and deterministic claims?
candidates.prior_work: Existing review calls for held-out units/conditions, uncertainty-aware measurements and explicit population coverage; no hardware dataset is present.
candidates.obstacle: Repeated measurements can share temperature and calibration errors; an empirical percentile is not an all-trajectories bound.
candidates.crossover_seed: Use hierarchical set calibration and adversarial holdouts by unit/condition rather than row-wise random splits.
candidates.cheap_test: Create a small exact synthetic shared-bias example showing row-wise replication reduces naive uncertainty while leaving between-unit uncertainty unchanged.

candidates.title: Travel containment versus maintained rest
candidates.question: What additional controller and contract are needed to guarantee two-sided travel and explicit residual-motion tolerances after the finite first-zero maneuver?
candidates.prior_work: Latest finite handoff gives a forward ceiling, not lower travel, infinite holding or precision rest; an exact zero-speed positive-acceleration witness exposes the distinction.
candidates.obstacle: First velocity zero is neither standstill nor a maintained stop; negative braking can reverse direction.
candidates.crossover_seed: Use viability kernels in position/velocity/acceleration and terminal-set design with a dwell-time motion predicate.
candidates.cheap_test: Propagate the first-zero state under unchanged braking and construct the earliest backward-travel violation, then derive the necessary hold-switch reserve.

candidates.title: Uncertainty-preserving action under ambiguous attribution
candidates.question: Can a safety decision remain sound when source attribution stays nonidentifiable and sensor observations contain duplicated shared information?
candidates.prior_work: Exact-rational synthetic example retains a joint feasible set, rejects an empty set and distinguishes compatibility from all-state guarantee; no dynamic stop-model bridge exists.
candidates.obstacle: Point estimates or falsely independent duplicated constraints can manufacture confidence; hull intersection can hide disconnected infeasibility.
candidates.crossover_seed: Transfer epistemic logic and abstract interpretation: act on every retained world, and make duplicate evidence idempotent.
candidates.cheap_test: Compare an exact union-of-polyhedra feasible set with its interval hull on a held-out observation that intersects the hull but no actual branch.
